When James announced his "last decision," several of his new teammates did not even bother to contain their excitement.

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley already wants to make plans on the links, as well.

James, 41, is reportedly signing a two-year, $8 million deal, taking a major discount, to join the 76ers, ESPN first reported.

James announced his decision in a post on X where he said he thought he was done at the end of last season and that he had likely played his final game. However, "I still truly love this game, and I have more to give."

LEBRON JAMES MAKES NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION, ANNOUNCES PLANS TO SIGN WITH 76ERS

The 76ers will be the fourth team James has played for in his illustrious career. For Philadelphia, James is the second major star to join the team this offseason, as they acquired Jaylen Brown in a stunning trade with the Boston Celtics earlier this month.

Last season, the 76ers were swept by the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference semifinals, and they hope the additions of James and Brown can propel them to a championship.

While James may not be the force he once was, he still remains a productive player going into his 24th season. In 60 games with the Los Angeles Lakers last season, James averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds per game and was named an All-Star for the 22nd time, extending his NBA record.

Fox News' Ryan Canfield contributed to this report.

item.title: James Carville blasts far-left 'White turds' among Dems who he says value Lenin more than MLK
item.description: James Carville warned democratic socialists value communist leader Vladimir Lenin over Martin Luther King Jr. and calls far-left politicians paternalistic on his podcast.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville condemned far-left Democrats on Thursday, warning that they value Soviet dictators more than American civil rights leaders.

During his "Politics War Room" podcast, Carville paraphrased a quote from an unnamed Democratic politician who had suggested that even Black American leaders are part of American imperialism. Carville responded with sarcasm, highlighting what he described as the absurdity that past civil rights leaders like John Lewis or Martin Luther King Jr. were puppets of such a system.

"These people are paternalistic, and it's a bunch of overeducated little White turds who think they know more than other people know, and they know what's wrong," Carville said of liberal politicians who would voice such an opinion.

JAMES CARVILLE WORRIES ABOUT THE 'END OF THE TWO-PARTY SYSTEM' AS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS GAIN POPULARITY

Carville has spent years warning the Democratic Party to distance itself from far-left culture-war politics. In recent months, with the rise of democratic socialists, however, Carville has gone so far as to suggest the party should have a schism to keep radicals from taking power.

On Thursday, he also recalled other socialist politicians taking far-left positions ranging from calls to indict Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to speaking out against interracial dating.

"Let me tell you something," Carville began, offering a warning to Black voters and to other more centrist liberals like himself, "They think they know more than you do. They think their history is more glorious than [yours] was. They think that Lenin was a more glorious human being than Martin Luther King or Frederick Douglass. That's what they really think."

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST IN HOT SEAT AGAIN OVER DELETED POSTS PRAISING COMMUNISM, MARXISM: 'CRAZYPANTS'

"And if you don't know that, you don't know your history. And you should view these people with extreme, extreme skepticism, because they think they know what's better for you than you know what's better for you," he warned. "And they think they know your history better than you. You know their history. This a--hole don't know what he's talking about."

"Someday James is going to tell us what he really thinks," his co-host Al Hunt joked.

"You can see this coming," Carville continued, warning, "It's always been ... they’ve got to be part of the movement. The only movement they got is a f---ing bowel movement."

Earlier this month, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) revealed a radical and controversial policy platform that sparked widespread backlash. Among the proposals were calls for an "immediate end to all deportations," free migration between countries without restrictive immigration controls, and "extending full voting rights to people with criminal convictions and noncitizens." 

In addition, the group called for the U.S. Senate to be abolished.

The latest Fox News Poll released Wednesday found that support for socialism is growing in the Democratic Party and has surpassed support for capitalism. By an 11-point margin, more Democrats have a favorable opinion of socialism (52%) than capitalism (41%), while by a 50-point margin, more Republicans have a positive view of capitalism (61%) than socialism (11%).

item.title: Alveda King slams USA Today columnist for invoking Emmett Till in Caitlin Clark piece: 'Pure race-baiting'
item.description: Alveda King calls Nancy Armour's USA Today column linking Emmett Till to Caitlin Clark's WNBA impact predictable race-baiting designed to stir emotion.
item.content:encoded:
At her age, race activist Alveda King wasn't the least bit surprised by the Caitlin Clark opinion piece penned this week by USA Today sports columnist Nancy Armour.

"I've seen every kind of race-baiting that you can imagine. I'm 75 years old," the niece of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. told OutKick on Friday. Armour's column relating the murder of Emmett Till to Caitlin Clark putting black and lesbian WNBA players in physical danger didn't come as a shock to a woman who has seen so much over her lifetime.

King, a Fox News contributor, says this playbook by the left-wing media is all too predictable.

"What people have learned to do, is to throw out inflammatory, emotional phrases that will make people emotional and forget how to think. There was no reason to throw Emmett Till's name out there. And so, that's called race-baiting," she continued.

King's advice to Americans is simple: Don't be "misled by emotional turmoil without examining the facts."

What are the facts here?

NANCY ARMOUR'S DISASTROUS CAITLIN CLARK ARTICLE EXEMPLIFIES WHY SPORTSWRITING AND SPORTS MEDIA IS FAILING

As OutKick's Dan Zaksheske has written this week, Armour has used Clark as a race-baiting target in the past. In 2024, the USA Today columnist wrote that Clark needed to "call out the toxic segment of her fan base" after an incident with DiJonai Carrington that left the Indiana Fever guard with a black eye. For some reason, Armour made Clark the villain in the situation.

This season, Armour alleges, Clark is egging on her supporters to send nasty messages to WNBA players by flopping and berating refs over no-calls. Armour's narrative is clear as day: Clark is a problem because she's white, straight, and a huge swath of America believes she's the best player in the WNBA.

Surely, Nancy has reached out to civil rights pundits and race historians, right?

"No, I have not," King said when asked if she's ever heard from Armour.

USA TODAY COLUMNIST WHO ATTACKED CAITLIN CLARK GOES AFTER HERITAGE FOUNDATION 'COMING FOR' TITLE IX

What about anyone from the USA Today Sports department? "I have not," King responded.

Have any editors ever called to add substance, or even alternative viewpoints to what Armour is pushing? "I don't know if they want to call me. You know, they've not called me, and I imagine if I tried to call them, I hope they would answer. I have no problem with having the same discussion," she continued.

OutKick reached out to the NAACP national office for this story on Thursday to add its own perspective. We have not heard back.

As for Armour, on Thursday, she released a statement on her column that was painted by USA Today as some sort of apology. "In my recent column, I made an inartful comparison with the murder of Emmett Till. I intended to connect the issues the WNBA is currently facing with its All-Star Game being hosted in Till's hometown of Chicago," Armour wrote. "I obviously did not provide enough context for that."

item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark was seen speaking with former President Barack Hussein Obama at WNBA All-Star Weekend in Chicago on Friday.

She later revealed what the conversation was while speaking to reporters.

"He just complimented me for the way I handle everything. Obviously with everything going on, and he's certainly someone who's been in front of the media quite a bit. And he reminded me, he's like 'I got famous in my 40s, I didn't have to do it in my 20s,'" Clark said.

CAITLIN CLARK MAKES WNBA HISTORY WITH RECORD-BREAKING GAME AFTER WEEKS OF CONTROVERSY

"And you know, sometimes, I think people don't always realize I'm 23 or 24 years old and trying to navigate a lot of different things, while trying to play basketball at the same time. So it was cool to hear that from him. And I think honestly it's probably a good reminder to all of us to treat people with respect and treat people with grace."

Footage of the interaction between Clark and Obama was also published by multiple media outlets in attendance.

In the footage by NBC Chicago, Obama appeared to be meeting Clark for the very first time, saying "really nice to meet you. You're great. You're fantastic," as he shook Clark's hand.

USA TODAY WRITER INVOKES EMMETT TILL, SAYS CAITLIN CLARK PUTS BLACK AND QUEER PLAYERS 'IN DANGER' BY FLOPPING

Immediately after that, the 44th president referenced the ongoing controversy surrounding Clark and the WNBA in recent weeks.

"Don't let all this nonsense get you down. I always say, one of the things that was luckiest for me is, I didn't get famous until I was like 45. So I was an old a-- man. I mean, you're my daughter's age... So don't lose that joy. The game's like the game. And you're a hooper."

Then they took a picture together, and Clark insisted that other WNBA players join in the picture with them.

Obama is considered one of the more controversial presidents in modern American history.

Meanwhile, Clark has been at the center of the biggest controversy in sports in recent weeks after getting punched in the throat by an opposing player. The WNBA has faced a maelstrom of controversy surrounding Clark and other players since then. The controversies often spark emotional viral debates that venture into discussions about racism and sexual orientation.

The controversy came to a head this week when an opinion writer for USA Today published a column that invoked the murder of Emmett Till while criticizing Clark for falling to the floor when hit by opposing players and arguing with referees over foul calls. The column has since drawn immense backlash from both sides of the political aisle, prompting the author to issue a statement that included an apology.

item.title: Diddy sent to solitary confinement after prison fight with another inmate: multiple reports
item.description: Sean Diddy Combs was reportedly sent to solitary confinement at FCI Fort Dix after a physical altercation with another inmate during his 50-month sentence.
item.content:encoded:
Sean "Diddy" Combs was sent to solitary confinement after he was involved in a fight with another inmate in the prison where he’s serving a 50-month term, according to several reports.

The rapper was convicted last year on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution and is serving his sentence at Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Fort Dix in New Jersey.

The 56-year-old was found guilty a year ago and began serving his sentence at Fort Dix in October.

The fight started after the other inmate made some kind of comment to the "I’ll Be Missing You" rapper, ABC News reported.

The music mogul "held his own" during the physical fight that was quickly stopped by staff, TMZ reported, citing multiple sources.

It’s unclear if the other inmate was also thrown in solitary as well.

Combs was moved to the low-security prison after his sentencing because of its drug rehab program and its proximity to his family.

Combs’ high-profile trial last year included testimony from his former girlfriend Casandra "Cassie" Ventura, who claimed he had subjected her to repeated physical abuse, rape and forced sexual encounters involving drugs during their relationship.

A rep for Combs told Fox News Digital he had no comment.
